items.title: 15.7 Effects of drugs on nervous coordination

source_refs.note: Topic 15.7 with its For Information box (PDF 46-47).

blocks.text: A drug is any substance, other than food, used to prevent, diagnose, treat or relieve the symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition. Drugs can also affect the brain and change mood, awareness, thoughts, feelings or behaviour.

items: Psychoactive drug: a drug that alters brain function, changing mood, perception, consciousness and behaviour, for example alcohol, caffeine, nicotine and illicit drugs such as cocaine and heroin.
Narcotic: an opioid drug used for pain relief that has a high potential for addiction and abuse, such as morphine, codeine and oxycodone.

blocks.title: Narcotics and psychoactive drugs
blocks.text: All narcotics are psychoactive drugs, but not all psychoactive drugs are narcotics.

blocks.explanation: No. Caffeine is psychoactive (it changes alertness) but it is not an opioid pain-reliever, so it is not a narcotic.

items: Drug: non-food substance to prevent, diagnose, treat or relieve. Psychoactive drugs alter brain function; narcotics are addictive opioid pain-relievers.
